speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: The reason why I have been asking this is also because residents have been experiencing a lot of noise along the Tampines Expressway (TPE) and in the night as well, in the wee hours.

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: I have been receiving a lot of feedback, residents sharing with me, and often times, they email me late, in the wee hours of the morning.

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: And I wonder if the Ministry would consider expediting the use of noise reducing road surfaces.

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: And post completion, when the viaduct is completed, whether there will be post-completion monitoring and additional mitigation measures, if let us say the noise levels exceed what residents can reasonably live with.

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: Lastly, I would also like to ask if the Ministry will be willing to explore enhanced soundproofing measures such as improved window treatments or insulation.

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: And whether when they plan new highways and road expansions, do they consider the impact of the well-being of the residents who live around the area?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But it is about taking a balance of cost, about technical feasibilities and also using very measurable tangible measures because residents' noise tolerance levels could differ from person to person.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We look at existing noise limits that are set by the relevant authorities.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the Day and Notice of Motion.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
